info.title: Selly API
info.summary: Bitcoin-only social commerce: storefronts, a sales agent in a website chat, Lightning payments on each vendor's own wallet, and sats subscriptions.
info.description:
Contract between `apps/web`, `apps/agent` and `apps/core`. Companion to `docs/architecture.md` (v0.3). While this file is written by hand it and the architecture document MUST agree; once `packages/contracts` generates it, the generated file wins.

**Conventions.** JSON with snake_case keys. Identifiers are UUIDv7. Time is RFC 3339 in UTC. Money is `{"amount": 15000, "currency": "XOF"}` in integer units; sats are integers named `*_sat` (`*_msat` where NWC uses millisats). Phone numbers are E.164. Nostr public keys are 64 lowercase hex characters.

**Errors** are RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` with a stable `code`.

**Idempotency.** `Idempotency-Key` is required on `POST /orders`, `POST /checkout/{token}/invoice`, `POST /vendors/me/subscription/invoices`, `POST /inventory`, `POST /inventory/restock-ai` and their internal twins. A replay within 24 hours returns the stored response. The same key with a different body returns 422 `IDEMPOTENCY_MISMATCH`. Chat messages use the body field `client_message_id`.

**Authentication.** Customers need no account: checkout endpoints are addressed by `public_token`, and the chat uses a bearer token from `POST /chat/sessions`. Vendors sign in with a signed Nostr challenge and get the `selly_session` cookie. Replacing the wallet or the keys needs a step-up (a signature less than 10 minutes old). Internal endpoints use a service token with scopes; core calls the agent with an HMAC signature.

**Examples** use BTC = 90,000 EUR, so 59,036,130 XOF per BTC. Invoices and keys in examples are well-formed but not payable or real.

**Routing on one domain.** `/api/v1/chat/*`, `/api/v1/conversations*` and `/api/v1/assistant*` are served by the agent. Other `/api/v1/*` paths are served by core. `/internal/*` is never routed from the internet.

post.summary: Get a one-time challenge to sign
post.description: Returns a random 32-byte challenge valid for 5 minutes and an `event_template` (kind 27235, NIP-98) for the signer to complete. For `step_up` and `add_key` the call needs the session cookie. The challenge can be used once.

post.summary: Sign in with the signed challenge event
post.description: Core checks, in order: the Schnorr signature and event id; `kind` 27235; `created_at` within 60 seconds; the `u` tag equals this endpoint's URL and the `method` tag equals `POST`; the `challenge` tag matches an unused, unexpired challenge of the right purpose, which is marked used in the same statement. On success sets the `selly_session` cookie. A key with no vendor yet gets `vendor: null`; `POST /vendors` then creates the shop. For a `step_up` challenge the open session gets `step_up_expires_at` 10 minutes ahead.

Set-Cookie.example: selly_session=Zk3p...; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Path=/; Max-Age=2592000

put.summary: Link or replace the vendor wallet
put.description: Steps: parse the URI; read the wallet info event; call `get_info`; apply the permission policy (must include `make_invoice` and `lookup_invoice`, must not include any spending method); create a 1-sat test invoice that expires in 60 seconds and look it up; encrypt and store the URI; write the audit record `wallet.linked` or `wallet.replaced`; push a notice to the dashboard. The URI is never returned, logged or sent to the browser again. Replacing an existing wallet needs a step-up.

post.summary: Send a message
post.description: Stores the message and answers 202 at once. The agent's reply, any vendor reply and system messages arrive on `GET /chat/events`. A repeated `client_message_id` returns the stored message and does not run a second turn. Messages that arrive while a turn runs are merged into the next turn. Past the plan's reply quota the request is still accepted and the customer gets the fixed handoff reply on the stream. Audio needs a plan with voice notes (`FEATURE_NOT_IN_PLAN` otherwise).

post.summary: Check a vendor session cookie
post.description: Scope `auth:introspect`. Used by the agent for the inbox and assistant endpoints. Core hashes the cookie value; the agent caches a positive answer for 60 seconds. Always 200: an invalid session returns `valid: false`.

post.summary: Core delivers an event to the agent
post.description: Sent from the outbox dispatcher: at least once, ordered per key (the order id). Signed with `X-Selly-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex>`, HMAC-SHA256 over `<t>.<raw body>`, 5 minutes of tolerance. The agent answers 200 for an `event_id` it already saw (`duplicate: true`). Backoff on failure: 1 s, 5 s, 30 s, 2 min, 10 min, 1 h, then a dead letter and an alert. Every `order.*` event carries `order_id`, `number`, `channel`, `conversation_ref`, `total`, `total_sat` and `checkout_url`. `order.paid` makes the agent add a system message to the order's conversation.
